answer: Each identity opens one margin account on an island board, locking 120 credits against 80 at a 150 percent ratio. A price thread posts each epoch's reference price, so any auditor can recompute every ratio from it. Below 150 percent, a liquidator closes it, sells its jade bond, takes 20 credits, and strips its weight. Fees rise with simultaneous failures: the j-th costs 20 plus j minus 1, so the 1,000th pays 1,019 and 1,000 fakes pay 519,500 in fees. A cross-margin ring fails, since the board forbids netting collateral across accounts. One honest agent posts 120 once.
